Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
Heard Mr. A.C.Srivastava, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.
Perused the record.

This repeat application for bail has been filed by applicant Roshan seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 103 of 2021, under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S. Rohta, District Meerut, during the pendency of trial.
At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. submits that notice of this repeat application for bail has been served upon first informant opposite party 2 on 13.4.2023.

However, in spite of service of notice,
neither any counter affidavit has been filed by opposite party 2 nor anyone has put in appearance on Roshan vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151263469/

sentences.text:
For ready reference, the order dated 17.11.2022 is reproduced herein under:-
"Heard Mr. Bhavya Sahai, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A.
for State.

This application for bail has been filed applicant Roshan seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 103 of 2021, under sections 452, 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC,
Police Station- Rohta District Meerut during the pendency of trial.
Perused the record.

Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 4.7.2021 a belated F.I.R. dated 7.7.2021 was lodged by first informant namely, Smt.
Suman, which was registered as Case Crime No. 103 of 2021, under section 452, 376,
323, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station- Rohta District Meerut.
In the aforesaid F.I.R. four persons namely, Mhesh @ Kukku, Roshan, Ritik Raj Gautam, Amanraj Gautam have been nominated as named accused.
The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that named accused with common object dislodged the modesty of prosecutrix.
It is alleged that named accused assaulted the husband and daughter of first informant on account of which the daughter of first informant sustained injuries on her head.
After lodging of aforesaid F.I.R. Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.

During course of investigation, Investigating Officer examined first informant under section 161 Cr.P.C, who has supported the prosecution story as unfolded in the F.I.R.
Thereafter the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C,
wherein she has not only supported the F.I.R. but also detailed the manner of occurrence.

As per aforesaid statement of prosecutrix, named accused Roshan i.e.
applicant herein dislodged the modesty of prosecutrix by forcibly committing rape upon her.
Subsequently, prosecutrix was medically examined.
Prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor has not only supported the prosecution story aas unfolded in F.I.R but her statement under section 161 Cr.P.C.

The Doctor who examined the prosecutrix opined as follows:
"There is a recent evidence of physical as well as sexual assault However final opinion can be given after collected report"

sentences.text: Thereafter the statement of prosecutrix was recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein she has reiterated her earlier statement under section 161 Cr.P.C. as well as her statement before the Doctor.
During course of investigation, Investigating Officer recovered the High School certificate of prosecutrix wherein her date of birth is recorded as 5.1.2004.
The occurrence in question is alleged to have occurred on 4.7.2021.
As such, on the date of occurrence the prosecutrix was aged about 17 years and 9 months.
On the basis of above and other material collected by during course of investigation, which is substantially adverse to applicant, he opined to submit charge sheet dated.
Accordingly Investigating Officer submitted the charge sheet dated1.9.2021.
whereby appliacnt has been charge-sheeted under sections 452, 376, 323, 504 and 506 IPC and under Section 3/4 POCSO Act, whereas rest of the named accused have been exculpated.
Learned counsel for applicant contends that applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused but he is innocent.
It is then submitted by learned counsel for applicant that occurrence is alleged to have occurred on 4.7.2021.
However, the F.I.R. in respect of same was lodged on 7.7.2021 not by the prosecutrix but by the mother of prosecutrix.
As such F.I.R. is highly belated.
However, no explanation regarding delay in lodging the F.I.R. has been given either in the F.I.R. itself or in the statement of first informant as recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C.

Placing reliance upon judgement of Supreme Court in P. Rajagopal Vs. State of Tamilnadu, AIR 2019 SC 2866, he submits that since delay in lodging F.I.R. has not been explained, the prosecution of applicant itself cannot be maintained.

entities.text: P. Rajagopal Vs. State of Tamilnadu, AIR 2019 SC 2866
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is next contended that the prosecution story as unfolded in F.I.R. does not speak of commission of rape upon the prosecutrix.
It is well settled that though the F.I.R. is not to be treated as an encyclopedia of the prosecution case but it must disclose the basic prosecution case.

On the aforesaid premise, learned counsel for applicant contends that criminality alleged to have committed by applicant in the statement of prosecutrix as recorded under section 161/164 Cr.P.C.,
as explanation has been offered is unreliable as it goes beyond the prosecution case as unfolded in F.I.R. and secondly regarding such improvement in the statement of prosecutrix.
He, further submits that as per the material on record the prosecutrix is aged about 17 and 1/2 years.
Eye witness of occurrence do not support the statement of prosecutrix recorded under section 161/164 Cr.
P.C. Applicant is in jail since 9.7.2021.
As such, he has undergone more than one year and four months of incarceration.
In case applicant is enlarged on bail he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A has opposed this application.
He submits that applicant is named as well as charge-sheeted accused.
As such, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
It is then contended by leanred A.G.A that applicant is guilty of committing an offence which falls in the category of moral turpitude.
As per high school certificate, the age of the prosecutrix is 17 years and six monhts, therefore, the provisions of POCSO Act are squarely applicable in the present case.
Medical evidence as well as oral statements of the prosecutrix clearly implicate the applicant in the crime in question.
There is nothing on record to show false implication of applicant.
It is thus urged that present application is liable to be rejected.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not over come the same.

sentences.text: 3 Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, as well as complicity of applicant, accusation made coupled with the fact that medical evidence supports the prosecution story, the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under section 161/164 Cr.P.C. clearly implicate the applicant in the crime in question, but without making any comment on the merits of the case, no case for grant of indulgence by this Court is made out.
Application fails and is liable to be rejected.
It is accordingly rejected. "
Learned counsel for applicant submits that though applicant is a named and charge sheeted accused, yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
Statements of the first informant as well as the prosecutrix, who have deposed before Court below as P.W. 1 and P.W. 2 have already been recorded.

On the above premise, it is thus urged by the learned counsel for applicant that in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, then in that eventuality, it cannot be said that applicant shall terrorize the witnesses or tamper the course of trial.
On the above premise, he, therefore, submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
It is then contended by the learned counsel for applicant that prosecutrix in her deposition before Court below has not fully supported the F.I.R.
As per deposition of the prosecutrix, the case shall not travel beyond section 354 I.P.C.

In view of above,
the applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 09.07.2021.
As such, he has undergone more than 3 years and 5 months of incarceration.
The charge sheet/police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted against applicant.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
However, up to this stage, no such incriminating circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
It is thus urged by the learned counsel for applicant that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
Learned A.G.A. submits that the prosecutrix in her statement-in-chief has categorically and clearly stated that rape was committed upon her by the applicant Roshan.
Though the prosecutrix has been cross examined, the said statement of fact could not be dislodged by the defence.
On the above premise, the learned A.G.A. submits that no new good or sufficient ground has emerged.

Considering the age of the prosecutrix,
who was aged about 17 years and 6 months at the time of occurrence the nature and gravity of offence and the punishment for alleged offence, no sympathy be shown by Roshan vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others

4 this Court in favour of applicant.
As such, this repeat application is liable to be rejected.

When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.
Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for state, upon perusal of material brought on record, nature and gravity of offence, evidence,
complicity of the accused, accusation made and coupled with the fact that the objections raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to this repeat application for bail could not be dislodged by the learned counsel for applicant, therefore,
irrespective of the varied submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of this repeat application for bail, this Court does not find any new good or sufficient ground so as to enlarge the applicant on bail.
In view of above, this repeat application for bail fails and is liable to be dismissed.
It is, accordingly, dismissed.
